text.p: Zapata Corp said on Thursday that it reiterated its commitment to acquiring the rest of Envirodyne Industries Inc in a letter to Environdyne's chairman, Edward Gustafson.
Zapata's bid is contingent upon the election of its board slate at Envirodyne's annual shareholders meeting this week.

Zapata's letter told Gustafson that to allay any concern that it would not later proceed with its $70 million bid for the 59.6 percent of Envirodyne it does not own, the company pledged that if it withdrew the offer before November 15, 1997, one of its designees to the Envirodyne board would resign.
Zapata's remaining designees on the board would vote for a replacement director designated by the directors not affiliated with Zapata, the company said.
Envirodyne is a food-packing company based in Oak Brook, Ill. Its shares were up 1/16 to 6-3/4 in afternoon trading, while Zapata was down 1/8 to 4-1/4.

Also on Thursday, Zapata said it has retained an investment advisor to help with the possible sale of its marine protein division. The company also said is evaluating offers for its Bolivian oil and natural gas operation.
